summary: Robert Paget Dewhurst worked in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He earned an M.A. at the University of Oxford in 1888 and served there as University Lecturer in Hindustani in 1924.

Robert Ripley Moore was an Indologist and linguist who earned his B.A. at Bethel College (~1952–1956) and Ph.D. at the University of Michigan (~1959–1965). He taught at Mussoorie College and was Assistant Professor of Indo-Aryan Linguistics at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1965–1966).

Robert S. Ellwood worked in religious studies and Japanology. He studied at the University of Colorado (~1950–1954), Yale University (~1954–1957), and the University of Chicago under Mircea Eliade (~1964–1967), before holding a post at the University of Southern California (~1967–1997).

Robert S. Nelson is an archaeologist and historian who studied at Rice University (~1965–1969) and New York University (~1970–1978). He served as a professor at the University of Chicago (~1974–2005) and held a post at Yale University (~2005).

Robert S. P. Beekes worked in linguistics and Indology, studying at Leiden University (~1956–1969) under doctoral supervisor F. B. J. Kuiper (~1961–1969). He taught at Marnix Gymnasium and later held posts at Leiden University in 1973 and 1979.

Robert Schram worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He earned a Ph.D. and PD at the University of Vienna (1869–1874), later working as an assistant at the Geneva Observatory (1872–1873) and Militärgeographisches Institut (1887), before a post at Vienna (~1887).

Robert Sewell was an Indologist and historian who studied at Radley College. He served in the Indian Civil Service (~1868–1894), as Keeper of the Tamil Nadu Archives, and as a Fellow at the University of Madras (~1887).

Robert Seymour Conway was a linguist who studied at the City of London School (~1877–1883). He held academic posts at Newnham College, Cambridge (~1887–1893) and Gonville and Caius College (~1888–1894).

Robert Tegethoff is an Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar, linguist, and Indologist. He earned an M.A. at the University of Cologne (2015–2018), worked as a Wissenschaftlicher Mitarbeiter at the Free University of Berlin (attested 2026), and secured a postdoc there in 2026.
Robert Vane Russell worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Trinity College, Cambridge (~1891–1895) and served in the Indian Civil Service from ~1895 to 1915.
Robert Warren Clark is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under doctoral supervisor Karen Christina Lang and adviser K. L. Seshagiri Rao (both attested 1994).

Robert Watson Frazer was an Indologist who studied at Rathmines School and Trinity College Dublin (~1872–1876) under Robert Atkinson. He served in the Indian Civil Service (~1876–1886) and lectured in Telugu and Tamil at UCL (1885–1916) and SOAS (1917–1919).
Robert Wilson Ievers worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He earned an M.A. from Queen's University Belfast and served in the Ceylon Civil Service starting in 1872.

Robert Xavier Murphy worked in Indology, linguistics, history, and archaeology. He served as a master at the Bombay Native Education Society (~1830) and as secretary of the Bombay Chamber of Commerce and Industry in 1839.

Robert Zimmermann was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at St Beuno's (1903–1907) and under Heinrich Lüders at Humboldt University of Berlin (1908–1913, Ph.D.). He served as professor at St. Xavier's College, Mumbai (1914–1930) and directed the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute.

Robert Zydenbos specializes in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at Utrecht University (~1975–1983) and held posts at the University of Toronto (~1999–2000), the University of Munich (~2001–2023), and the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2026).

Robert van Gulik worked in Sinology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Leiden University (1930) and Utrecht University (1930–1935, Ph.D.) under Jan Gonda, C. C. Uhlenbeck, and J. J. L. Duyvendak, becoming Professor of Far Eastern Cultural History at Utrecht in 1967.

Robert von Heine-Geldern, a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology, studied at Munich (1903) and Vienna (~1910–1914) under Wilhelm Schmidt. He held posts at the University of Vienna (1925, 1931, 1949, 1955–1958), Columbia University (1938–1941), and the Asia Institute (1943–1949).

Robert von Schlagintweit was a scholar in history and archaeology who studied at the University of Munich (~1850–1854). He served as Professor of Geography at the University of Giessen starting in 1864.

Robin Coningham is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who completed his Ph.D. at King's College, Cambridge (~1989–1994) under Frank Raymond Allchin. He held professorships at the University of Bradford (1994–2005) and Durham University (appointed 2005).
